# I'd like more definition between header and articles on the docs viewer sidebar

![19087.png](assets/19087.png)
Currently the headers for the article categories are almost identical to the article names.

Can you please make them more pronounced and maybe collapsible for the ones under it so it's easier to scroll through. Feel free to reorganise if wanted to make the categories make sense more especially now we are leaning into the groupings

Read text file `docs/tasks/68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md — Docs viewer sidebar: definition between headers and articles
2|
3|## 1. Goal
4|
5|Give the docs viewer sidebar (`frontend/src/components/docs/DocsView.jsx`)
6|clear visual separation between category headers and article names, make each
7|category collapsible, and reorganise the two current avenues
8|(`how-it-works` / `working-with`) into groupings that match how the docs are
9|actually used — implementing the survey-chosen style:
10|
11|- **Chosen design (SURVEY.md r1/q5):** dark sidebar, category headers as small
12|  rounded badge labels with soft purple background and dark text, article names
13|  in lighter grey indented underneath, arrow on each header to collapse the
14|  group — "modern app look" (`assets/survey-r1-q5-chosen.png`).
15|- **Survey mandates locked in:** totally-new sidebar style is approved (q1);
16|  every category collapsible (q2); collapsed state persists across visits (q3,
17|  i.e. `localStorage`); articles may be freely regrouped/renamed (q4).
18|
19|Current pain (from `assets/19087.png`): headers are 10px mono uppercase grey
20|(`text-text-muted`) sitting directly above same-size article buttons, so the
21|two levels scan as one flat list; with ~9 articles under "How KainBain works"
22|and ~25+ under "How to work with KainBain", the long second group dominates
23|scrolling.
24|
25|## 2. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change
26|
27|Phases A–C below change no pixels: they isolate the sidebar, centralise the
28|taxonomy, and lock behaviour with tests so the visual/collapse/regroup work
29|(Phase D) lands as small, reversible edits on a seam built for it. Do not
30|start Phase D until A–C are green.
31|
32|## 3. Current-state facts (researched this run)
33|
34|- Sidebar source: `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsView.jsx` lines ~199–259 —
35|  `DOC_SECTION_LABELS`, `DOC_SECTION_ORDER`, `grouped` memo, and the inline
36|  `<section>/<h2>/<ul>` render loop. Headers are plain `h2`, not buttons.
37|- Taxonomy source of truth: `api/siteDocs.js` — `DOC_SECTIONS`,
38|  `SECTION_LABELS`, frontmatter `section:` per file in `site-docs/*.md`.
39|  Frontend duplicates the labels in `DOC_SECTION_LABELS`; the two copies must be
40|  changed together (or unified — see Step 2).
41|- Behavioural contracts in tests that constrain the work:
42|  - `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsView.test.jsx` — both avenues listed,
43|    filter, empty/error/XSS states, bare-`/docs` normalisation, deep links,
44|    and the **heading-order test** (`sidebar avenue headings are h2`).
45|    Collapsible headers become interactive, so this test must evolve, not
46|    break silently (see Step 7).
47|  - `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsNavigation.test.jsx` — docs routing
48|    regression lock (leaving docs, refresh, back/forward). Collapse state must
49|    never touch the route.
50|- Imbalance to fix: `grep ^section: site-docs/*.md` shows the `working-with`
51|  avenue holding onboarding, runners, auth, skills, runbooks, and reference
52|  alike — the regroup in Step 4 is data-driven, not a guess.
53|- Verification gates: `npm run test:frontend` (vitest incl. both suites above),
54|  `npm run lint:frontend`, headless check via `npm run capture:screenshot`
55|  (no long-lived dev servers per stage guidance).
56|
57|## 4. Step-by-step work plan
58|
59|### PHASE A — Seams first (no visual change)
60|
61|**Step 1 — Extract a `DocsSidebarGroup` component (frontend-only refactor).**
62|Move the per-group `<section>/<h2>/<ul>` block out of `DocsView.jsx` into a
63|new `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsSidebarGroup.jsx` taking
64|`{ label, docs, activeSlug, onSelect }` and rendering the *identical* markup.
65|`DocsView.jsx` keeps `DOC_SECTION_ORDER`/`grouped` and maps groups to the new
66|component. Pure move; no class changes.
67|*Why first:* every later step (badges, chevron button, collapsed rendering)
68|edits one small component instead of the 343-line view.
69|
70|**Step 2 — Single-source the taxonomy.**
71|Export the section list/labels from one place both layers already respect
72|(e.g. have the frontend import the API's `DOC_SECTIONS`/`SECTION_LABELS`
73|shape via the docs-index response, or a shared `docsSections` module) and
74|delete the `DocsView.jsx` duplicate. Add/extend a unit test asserting frontend
75|labels equal API labels for every section.
76|*Why first:* regrouping (Step 4) then touches frontmatter + one constant, not
77|two files that can drift.
78|
79|**Step 3 — Add the collapse-state hook with persistence.**
80|New hook (e.g. `useCollapsedSections`, co-located with the sidebar component):
81|`{ collapsed, toggle(section) }`, initialised from `localStorage`
82|(key e.g. `kainbain.docsSidebar.collapsed.v1`, JSON array of section ids,
83|`try/catch` around parse for corrupt values), writing back on change.
84|Unit-test the hook standalone: default-expanded, toggle flips one section,
85|corrupt storage falls back to expanded, choice survives remount.
86|*Why first:* persistence (survey q3) is the fiddliest behaviour; proving it in
87|isolation keeps the UI step dumb.
88|
89|### PHASE B — Safety net before pixels
90|
91|**Step 4 — Decide the new grouping from the data.**
92|Audit all `site-docs/*.md` frontmatter (`title/section/order`) and cluster
93|into 3–4 groups sized for scanning, e.g. *Getting started* (getting-started,
94|install-run, first-time-setup, link-runner-*, first-project), *Concepts*
95|(architecture, pipeline-stages, agent-execution, prompts-tokens, …),
96|*Everyday workflows* (editing-tasks, review-gates, custom-skills, …),
97|*Reference & runbooks* (api-reference, ports-env, git-index-lock-runbook,
98|surveys, …). Rule: no group holds more than ~10 articles; onboarding order
99|(concepts before operations) preserved. Write the proposed mapping as a table
100|in the implementing PR/task note and confirm it once — renames move `title:`
101|only, slugs stay stable so `/docs/:slug` deep links and the router tests never
102|break.
103|*Research-before-build:* this is the "big piece" the task calls out — do it
104|before any styling so Step 5 styles the real groups.
105|
106|**Step 5 — Characterisation tests for the new contract (red first).**
107|Extend `DocsView.test.jsx` / `DocsNavigation.test.jsx` (or a new
108|`DocsSidebarGroup.test.jsx`) with failing tests for: (a) each header renders
109|the badge style hook (assert via class/test-id, not pixels); (b) clicking a
110|header chevron collapses/expands only that group; (c) collapsed state persists
111|across remount (localStorage); (d) text filter auto-expands groups holding
112|matches and shows the empty-search state when none match; (e) active article
113|auto-expands its own group on deep link even if stored collapsed;
114|(f) collapse never changes the route (navigation-lock suite stays green);
115|(g) keyboard: header toggle reachable and operable via Tab+Enter/Space with
116|`aria-expanded`.
117|*Why before:* defines "done" for the visual step and protects the heading-order
118|and routing contracts while markup changes.
119|
120|### PHASE C — The change (small edits on the seams)
121|
122|**Step 6 — Apply the chosen badge style to `DocsSidebarGroup`.**
123|Header becomes the survey winner: pill/badge (`rounded-full`, soft purple
124|bg/dark text — reuse the existing `bg-primary`/`text-on-primary` tokens or the
125|accent-token companion in `frontend/src/theme/`, not a hardcoded hex),
126|articles `text-on-surface`/muted, indented (`pl-4`) under the badge, wider
127|spacing above each group (`mt-4 first:mt-0`), chevron (`Icon` chevron,
128|rotates 90° on collapse) beside the badge per `assets/survey-r1-q5-chosen.png`.
129|Keep the header text inside an `h2` with the toggle as the button *inside* it
130|(`<h2><button aria-expanded …>`), so the existing axe heading-order contract
131|holds by construction. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for the chevron/list
132|transition and keep the 44px touch targets.
133|
134|**Step 7 — Wire collapse + filter/deep-link interplay.**
135|Header button toggles via the Step-3 hook; collapsed groups render badge +
136|count only (`aria-expanded="false"`, list hidden). Rules: filter text forces
137|matching groups open (restore stored state on clear); deep link / active
138|article forces its group open on navigation; "Expand all / Collapse all" (if
139|added) is sidebar-scoped and separate from the existing article-section
140|controls. Update the old `sidebar avenue headings are h2` test to assert
141|`h2 > button[aria-expanded]` instead of a plain `h2` — an intentional,
142|reviewed contract evolution, documented in the commit message.
143|
144|**Step 8 — Migrate the taxonomy data.**
145|Change `section:` frontmatter per the Step-4 mapping, update `DOC_SECTIONS`/
146|`SECTION_LABELS` (API + the single-sourced frontend constant), keep
147|`order:` sequencing within each new group. Slugs unchanged. Run the
148|`siteDocs` API suites (`api/siteDocs*.test.js`, `routes/docs.test.js`,
149|`docs.apiCoverage`) — an unknown-section guard (`readDocFile` returns null)
150|means any missed file surfaces as a test failure, not a silent drop.
151|
152|### PHASE D — Assurance (prove it, then document it)
153|
154|**Step 9 — Automated verification.**
155|`npm run test:frontend` (both docs suites + new collapse/persistence tests),
156|`npm run test:api` (siteDocs suites after regroup), `npm run lint:frontend`,
157|plus the repo's contrast tests if badge tokens changed
158|(`frontend/src/theme/*contrast*`). Headless visual proof only:
159|`npm run capture:screenshot` of `/docs` (expanded, one-group-collapsed,
160|filtered states) attached to the task — no persistent dev servers.
161|
162|**Step 10 — Manual / accessibility pass.**
163|Keyboard-only run (Tab to header, Enter toggles, focus visible), screen-reader
164|spot check (group label + `aria-expanded` announced, article count exposed),
165|viewport sweep (narrow ~360px: badges wrap, no horizontal scroll; wide: sidebar
166|stays `w-64`), reduced-motion on/off, corrupt/empty `localStorage` entry,
167|filter-while-collapsed, deep link into a stored-collapsed group.
168|
169|**Step 11 — Documentation updates.**
170|Update whichever of these describe the sidebar/taxonomy: the docs-viewer
171|section of the relevant `site-docs/*.md` (e.g. getting-started or
172|stage/UX-adjacent article), `site-docs/README.md` template frontmatter comment
173|if sections are enumerated there, and the `DOC_SECTIONS`/`SECTION_LABELS`
174|docblocks in `api/siteDocs.js` if the avenue description changes. Note the new
175|`localStorage` key and the regroup mapping in the change notes so support can
176|answer "where did article X go".
177|
178|## 5. Risks and mitigations
179|
180|- **Two taxonomies drift (frontend labels vs API sections):** killed by Step 2's
181|  single source + equality test.
182|- **Heading-order a11y regression (plain `h2` → interactive header):**
183|  `h2 > button` pattern + evolved (not deleted) heading test + axe/manual
184|  reader check in Step 10.
185|- **Collapsed group hides the deep-linked/active article:** active slug always
186|  forces its group open (Step 7e); covered by test.
187|- **Filter + collapse confusion:** filter overrides collapse while typed,
188|  restores on clear (Step 7); empty-search state retained.
189|- **localStorage unavailable/corrupt (private mode, SSR):** `try/catch`,
190|  default expanded, never throws (Step 3 test).
191|- **Regroup orphaning an article:** `readDocFile` unknown-section null +
192|  API suites fail loudly; slugs frozen so routes/bookmarks survive (Step 8).
193|- **Badge contrast failure:** reuse theme tokens, run contrast suites
194|  (Step 9); fall back to the q5 option-0 high-spacing style if tokens fail.
195|
196|## 6. Non-goals
197|
198|- No change to article rendering, `MarkdownViewer`, or article-level
199|  expand/collapse; no search-backend work (title filter only); no route
200|  changes; no new dependencies or icon set — reuse `Icon` + theme tokens.

25|## 2. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change
26|

28|taxonomy, and lock behaviour with tests so the visual/collapse/regroup work

38|  `SECTION_LABELS`, frontmatter `section:` per file in `site-docs/*.md`.

40|  changed together (or unified — see Step 2).

42|  - `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsView.test.jsx` — both avenues listed,
43|    filter, empty/error/XSS states, bare-`/docs` normalisation, deep links,
44|    and the **heading-order test** (`sidebar avenue headings are h2`).
45|    Collapsible headers become interactive, so this test must evolve, not
46|    break silently (see Step 7).
47|  - `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsNavigation.test.jsx` — docs routing
48|    regression lock (leaving docs, refresh, back/forward). Collapse state must
49|    never touch the route.

51|  avenue holding onboarding, runners, auth, skills, runbooks, and reference
52|  alike — the regroup in Step 4 is data-driven, not a guess.
53|- Verification gates: `npm run test:frontend` (vitest incl. both suites above),
54|  `npm run lint:frontend`, headless check via `npm run capture:screenshot`
55|  (no long-lived dev servers per stage guidance).

57|## 4. Step-by-step work plan
58|
59|### PHASE A — Seams first (no visual change)
60|
61|**Step 1 — Extract a `DocsSidebarGroup` component (frontend-only refactor).**
62|Move the per-group `<section>/<h2>/<ul>` block out of `DocsView.jsx` into a
63|new `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsSidebarGroup.jsx` taking
64|`{ label, docs, activeSlug, onSelect }` and rendering the *identical* markup.
65|`DocsView.jsx` keeps `DOC_SECTION_ORDER`/`grouped` and maps groups to the new
66|component. Pure move; no class changes.
67|*Why first:* every later step (badges, chevron button, collapsed rendering)
68|edits one small component instead of the 343-line view.
69|
70|**Step 2 — Single-source the taxonomy.**
71|Export the section list/labels from one place both layers already respect
72|(e.g. have the frontend import the API's `DOC_SECTIONS`/`SECTION_LABELS`
73|shape via the docs-index response, or a shared `docsSections` module) and
74|delete the `DocsView.jsx` duplicate. Add/extend a unit test asserting frontend
75|labels equal API labels for every section.
76|*Why first:* regrouping (Step 4) then touches frontmatter + one constant, not
77|two files that can drift.
78|
79|**Step 3 — Add the collapse-state hook with persistence.**
80|New hook (e.g. `useCollapsedSections`, co-located with the sidebar component):
81|`{ collapsed, toggle(section) }`, initialised from `localStorage`
82|(key e.g. `kainbain.docsSidebar.collapsed.v1`, JSON array of section ids,
83|`try/catch` around parse for corrupt values), writing back on change.
84|Unit-test the hook standalone: default-expanded, toggle flips one section,
85|corrupt storage falls back to expanded, choice survives remount.
86|*Why first:* persistence (survey q3) is the fiddliest behaviour; proving it in
87|isolation keeps the UI step dumb.

89|### PHASE B — Safety net before pixels
90|
91|**Step 4 — Decide the new grouping from the data.**
92|Audit all `site-docs/*.md` frontmatter (`title/section/order`) and cluster
93|into 3–4 groups sized for scanning, e.g. *Getting started* (getting-started,
94|install-run, first-time-setup, link-runner-*, first-project), *Concepts*
95|(architecture, pipeline-stages, agent-execution, prompts-tokens, …),
96|*Everyday workflows* (editing-tasks, review-gates, custom-skills, …),
97|*Reference & runbooks* (api-reference, ports-env, git-index-lock-runbook,
98|surveys, …). Rule: no group holds more than ~10 articles; onboarding order
99|(concepts before operations) preserved. Write the proposed mapping as a table
100|in the implementing PR/task note and confirm it once — renames move `title:`
101|only, slugs stay stable so `/docs/:slug` deep links and the router tests never
102|break.
103|*Research-before-build:* this is the "big piece" the task calls out — do it
104|before any styling so Step 5 styles the real groups.

106|**Step 5 — Characterisation tests for the new contract (red first).**
107|Extend `DocsView.test.jsx` / `DocsNavigation.test.jsx` (or a new
108|`DocsSidebarGroup.test.jsx`) with failing tests for: (a) each header renders
109|the badge style hook (assert via class/test-id, not pixels); (b) clicking a
110|header chevron collapses/expands only that group; (c) collapsed state persists
111|across remount (localStorage); (d) text filter auto-expands groups holding
112|matches and shows the empty-search state when none match; (e) active article
113|auto-expands its own group on deep link even if stored collapsed;
114|(f) collapse never changes the route (navigation-lock suite stays green);
115|(g) keyboard: header toggle reachable and operable via Tab+Enter/Space with
116|`aria-expanded`.
117|*Why before:* defines "done" for the visual step and protects the heading-order
118|and routing contracts while markup changes.
119|
120|### PHASE C — The change (small edits on the seams)
121|
122|**Step 6 — Apply the chosen badge style to `DocsSidebarGroup`.**
123|Header becomes the survey winner: pill/badge (`rounded-full`, soft purple
124|bg/dark text — reuse the existing `bg-primary`/`text-on-primary` tokens or the
125|accent-token companion in `frontend/src/theme/`, not a hardcoded hex),
126|articles `text-on-surface`/muted, indented (`pl-4`) under the badge, wider
127|spacing above each group (`mt-4 first:mt-0`), chevron (`Icon` chevron,
128|rotates 90° on collapse) beside the badge per `assets/survey-r1-q5-chosen.png`.
129|Keep the header text inside an `h2` with the toggle as the button *inside* it
130|(`<h2><button aria-expanded …>`), so the existing axe heading-order contract
131|holds by construction. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for the chevron/list
132|transition and keep the 44px touch targets.
133|
134|**Step 7 — Wire collapse + filter/deep-link interplay.**
135|Header button toggles via the Step-3 hook; collapsed groups render badge +
136|count only (`aria-expanded="false"`, list hidden). Rules: filter text forces
137|matching groups open (restore stored state on clear); deep link / active
138|article forces its group open on navigation; "Expand all / Collapse all" (if
139|added) is sidebar-scoped and separate from the existing article-section
140|controls. Update the old `sidebar avenue headings are h2` test to assert
141|`h2 > button[aria-expanded]` instead of a plain `h2` — an intentional,
142|reviewed contract evolution, documented in the commit message.
143|
144|**Step 8 — Migrate the taxonomy data.**
145|Change `section:` frontmatter per the Step-4 mapping, update `DOC_SECTIONS`/
146|`SECTION_LABELS` (API + the single-sourced frontend constant), keep
147|`order:` sequencing within each new group. Slugs unchanged. Run the
148|`siteDocs` API suites (`api/siteDocs*.test.js`, `routes/docs.test.js`,
149|`docs.apiCoverage`) — an unknown-section guard (`readDocFile` returns null)
150|means any missed file surfaces as a test failure, not a silent drop.
151|
152|### PHASE D — Assurance (prove it, then document it)
153|
154|**Step 9 — Automated verification.**
155|`npm run test:frontend` (both docs suites + new collapse/persistence tests),
156|`npm run test:api` (siteDocs suites after regroup), `npm run lint:frontend`,
157|plus the repo's contrast tests if badge tokens changed
158|(`frontend/src/theme/*contrast*`). Headless visual proof only:
159|`npm run capture:screenshot` of `/docs` (expanded, one-group-collapsed,
160|filtered states) attached to the task — no persistent dev servers.
161|
162|**Step 10 — Manual / accessibility pass.**
163|Keyboard-only run (Tab to header, Enter toggles, focus visible), screen-reader
164|spot check (group label + `aria-expanded` announced, article count exposed),
165|viewport sweep (narrow ~360px: badges wrap, no horizontal scroll; wide: sidebar
166|stays `w-64`), reduced-motion on/off, corrupt/empty `localStorage` entry,
167|filter-while-collapsed, deep link into a stored-collapsed group.
168|
169|**Step 11 — Documentation updates.**
170|Update whichever of these describe the sidebar/taxonomy: the docs-viewer
171|section of the relevant `site-docs/*.md` (e.g. getting-started or
172|stage/UX-adjacent article), `site-docs/README.md` template frontmatter comment
173|if sections are enumerated there, and the `DOC_SECTIONS`/`SECTION_LABELS`
174|docblocks in `api/siteDocs.js` if the avenue description changes. Note the new

176|answer "where did article X go".

178|## 5. Risks and mitigations
179|
180|- **Two taxonomies drift (frontend labels vs API sections):** killed by Step 2's
181|  single source + equality test.
182|- **Heading-order a11y regression (plain `h2` → interactive header):**
183|  `h2 > button` pattern + evolved (not deleted) heading test + axe/manual
184|  reader check in Step 10.
185|- **Collapsed group hides the deep-linked/active article:** active slug always
186|  forces its group open (Step 7e); covered by test.
187|- **Filter + collapse confusion:** filter overrides collapse while typed,
188|  restores on clear (Step 7); empty-search state retained.
189|- **localStorage unavailable/corrupt (private mode, SSR):** `try/catch`,
190|  default expanded, never throws (Step 3 test).
191|- **Regroup orphaning an article:** `readDocFile` unknown-section null +
192|  API suites fail loudly; slugs frozen so routes/bookmarks survive (Step 8).
193|- **Badge contrast failure:** reuse theme tokens, run contrast suites
194|  (Step 9); fall back to the q5 option-0 high-spacing style if tokens fail.
195|

197|
198|- No change to article rendering, `MarkdownViewer`, or article-level
199|  expand/collapse; no search-backend work (title filter only); no route
200|  changes; no new dependencies or icon set — reuse `Icon` + theme tokens.

1|# PR Review — docs viewer sidebar: header definition + collapsible groups (2026-11-16)
2|
3|Scope reviewed: branch `kb/68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393` vs `origin/main`
4|(merge-base `45b0db37`): `api/siteDocs.js`, `frontend/src/components/docs/DocsView.jsx`,
5|`DocsSidebarGroup.jsx`, `docsSections.js`, `useCollapsedSections.js`,
6|`frontend/src/components/Icon.jsx`, `frontend/tailwind.config.js`,
7|`site-docs/*.md` frontmatter, all touched tests, plus prior reports
8|(SURVEY, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, both audits, code-standards review, CI failures).
9|
10|## Verdict: PASS — suitable to integrate
11|
12|## 1. Does it achieve the goal?
13|Yes. The expanded proof screenshot shows exactly the survey-chosen style
14|(`SURVEY.md` r1/q5): category headers as lavender badge pills with article
15|counts and collapse chevrons, articles indented underneath in lighter text.
16|The 2-avenue imbalance is fixed by regrouping into 4 groups
17|(Getting started / Concepts / Everyday workflows / Reference & runbooks).
18|Every group collapses independently and persists via
19|`kainbain.docsSidebar.collapsed.v1` (`useCollapsedSections.js`).
20|
21|## 2. Did it follow the plan?
22|Yes. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN phases are traceable: seams first
23|(`DocsSidebarGroup.jsx`, `docsSections.js`, hook co-located with `DocsView.jsx`),
24|characterisation tests before pixels (`DocsSidebarGroup.test.jsx`,
25|`useCollapsedSections.test.jsx`, `docsSections.test.js`, `DocsView.test.jsx`
26|filter/deep-link/route-immutability cases), then badge styling, collapse wiring
27|(filter and active-article force-open, `pinnedClosedSlug`), then taxonomy
28|migration with slugs frozen. The `h2 > button[aria-expanded]` heading-order
29|evolution is documented in the test, as the plan required.
30|
31|## 3. Code standards?
32|PASS per `review-code-standards-20261116.md` (principle-by-principle, no
33|blocking violations). Corroborated by reading `DocsSidebarGroup.jsx`,
34|`DocsView.jsx`, and `useCollapsedSections.js` this run. Three recorded nits
35|(terse locals, stale `Icon.jsx` JSDoc union, storage write inside the state
36|updater) are advisory only.
37|
38|## 4. Easy to modify later?
39|Yes. One component per group, one hook owning stored state, taxonomy in
40|`docsSections.js` mirroring `api/siteDocs.js` and locked by
41|`api/siteDocs.frontendParity.test.js`. Backend-driven `sectionOrder` with
42|unknown-group append (`DocsView.jsx:191-216`) means future groups cannot
43|vanish silently.
44|
45|## 5. Best practices / 6. Tech debt?
46|No new debt. No new dependencies or icon set (reuses `Icon` + theme tokens),
47|collapse never touches the route, hostile-input guards throughout
48|(malformed index entries, corrupt/empty storage, quota failures all fall back
49|to expanded). Upgrade-safety re-audit (`upgrade-safety-audit-20261116.md`)
50|reproduced the old hard-rename break live and confirmed it closed via
51|`LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` + warning + `DEPRECATIONS.md` notice. The one full-CI
52|failure on record is unrelated to this change: a timing-sensitive
53|`runner/daemon.test.js` cadence assertion ("expected renewals, saw 1") plus
54|proof-PNG text-path corruption (see below).

58|authoring rules, `agents.md` / `api/agentGuide.js` copy, JSDoc `MARK` blocks
59|with `@example` on every new surface, and three proof screenshots attached.

TITLE: Enforce binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene
STAGE: stage-1794594754686 | STATUS: completed
GOAL: # Enforce binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene

## Context
Case study: KainBain task 5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f (pretty markdown tasks with code blocks, mermaid diagrams, and image references). A Deep Review stage failed the branch for two worktree-hygiene defects: docs proof file pretty-proof.png was byte-corrupted (magic bytes efbfbd instead of PNG magic 89504e47; the file tool reported data instead of PNG, contradicting the implementation report validity claim), and a stray dead scratch file rt.mjs with a broken import was committed at the repo root. See docs/tasks/5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f/deep-review-failure-20261114-093429.md and the round-3 review it cites. The likely mechanism is agents writing or rewriting binary files through text-oriented edit tools, plus committing ad-hoc scratch files instead of keeping them untracked or outside the repo.

## Steps
1. Add documented guidance for proof artifacts: binary files (PNG screenshots, etc.) must be written through a binary-safe path only, never through text edit tools; verify with magic bytes (89504e47 for PNG) and the file command before claiming validity.
2. Add a cheap automated check (CI step or pre-commit check) that rejects: (a) committed files at the repo root matching scratch patterns (*.mjs scratch, rt.*, etc.) unless explicitly allowlisted, and (b) files under docs proof paths whose magic bytes do not match their extension.
3. Correct the stale validity claim in the implementation report only if it is still wrong on the current branch; otherwise leave history untouched.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A corrupted PNG (wrong magic bytes) committed as proof fails the new check with a message naming the file and expected vs actual magic.
- [ ] A scratch file dropped at the repo root fails the new check or is blocked from commit.
- [ ] Valid PNG proof plus no stray root files passes the check.

## Notes
This ticket targets structural process failure (binary handling
